uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to capture information disclosure from stored personal content and metadata.

title: Video entries may be linkable across uploads, users, or services
description: If the stored video documents include persistent account identifiers, device IDs, IP-derived metadata, content hashes, or stable filenames, records in the collection may be linked to each other or to datasets from other systems, enabling profiling of individuals across uploads or contexts.
assumptions: The schema retains stable identifiers or quasi-identifiers that persist across transactions.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for linkability through persistent identifiers in stored records.

title: Indirect identification may be possible from video metadata and context
description: Even if direct identifiers are omitted, combinations of timestamps, geolocation, channel information, thumbnails, tags, or unique content characteristics in the stored records can allow a person to be singled out or re-identified.
assumptions: Stored metadata includes quasi-identifiers or rich contextual fields.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for indirect identifiability via combinations of attributes.

title: Insufficient evidence of consent or upload authorization for stored videos
description: If /api/videos writes video records without recording who submitted them, when, under what authority, and what consent or legal basis applied, the system may be unable to prove whether the upload was authorized or privacy choices were respected.
assumptions: The write path may not persist auditable consent, authorization, or provenance metadata alongside the record.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to capture non-repudiation gaps around privacy-relevant actions and consent evidence.

title: Users may be unaware that uploaded videos and metadata are persistently stored
description: The write operation stores videos in a database collection, but users or data subjects may not understand what exact fields are stored, how long they are retained, who can access them, or whether metadata is extracted and kept separately. This undermines predictability and awareness of processing.
assumptions: Privacy notices or in-product explanations may be incomplete or not specific to the stored data fields and retention.
uncertainty_note: Node id is best-effort for unawareness regarding storage, retention, and downstream use.

title: Stored videos may exceed purpose, minimization, or retention requirements
description: Writing full video payloads and rich metadata to the videos collection may conflict with data minimization, purpose limitation, or retention obligations if more data is stored than needed, retained too long, or reused for secondary purposes without a valid basis.
assumptions: The implementation may store raw content and metadata broadly or keep it beyond the original upload purpose.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; intended to represent non-compliance with privacy principles for storage and reuse.

title: Reading full video records may expose personal metadata to the API process
description: The /api/videos process reads video records from the MongoDB videos collection. If those records contain personal data such as uploader identity, viewing-related metadata, location, tags, or internal identifiers, the read operation allows the process to learn more personal information than is necessary for a given request, creating a disclosure risk.
assumptions: Assumes the videos collection includes personal or linkable metadata and that the API process or its outputs are not strictly minimized to only necessary fields.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a best-fit disclosure-from-data-store read; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may vary.

title: Video records may enable linking across requests or systems
description: Stable identifiers in the videos collection, such as video IDs, uploader IDs, channel IDs, or other persistent references, may allow /api/videos to correlate records across requests, users, or other datasets. This can link separate activities or identities that should remain less correlated.
assumptions: Assumes the collection contains persistent identifiers or quasi-identifiers and that /api/videos can combine or expose them across contexts.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort approximation for linkability via persistent identifiers in retrieved records.

title: Video metadata may reveal user or uploader identity
description: When /api/videos reads the videos collection, fields such as uploader name, account ID, profile references, embedded contact details, or distinctive content metadata may directly or indirectly identify a person.
assumptions: Assumes some video records are associated with natural persons or small groups and include direct or indirect identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit identifiability node; exact subnode may differ depending on whether identification is direct or indirect.

title: Broad reads from the videos collection may exceed data minimization
description: The /api/videos process may retrieve complete documents from the videos collection even when only a subset of fields is needed. Reading unnecessary fields increases dissemination risk within the system and may later propagate excess personal data to logs, caches, or responses.
assumptions: Assumes queries are not projection-limited and documents contain more personal data than required for the API purpose.
uncertainty_note: Mapped as a detectability/disclosure-related data minimization issue using best-fit LINDDUN Pro node; exact taxonomy placement may vary.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that stored video data is accessed via this API
description: The read path from the videos collection to /api/videos may not be transparent to uploaders or other affected individuals. If people are not informed that their video metadata or associated personal data is accessed for this API function, processing can become insufficiently transparent and thus unaware to data subjects.
assumptions: Assumes notices or in-product transparency about this access path are incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node; exact subnode depends on the specific transparency failure.

title: Reading videos from the collection may be incompatible with the original purpose or consent
description: If the videos collection was populated for storage, playback, or creator management purposes, using it through /api/videos for additional analytics, discovery, administrative, or other secondary purposes may violate purpose limitation, consent expectations, or other privacy obligations.
assumptions: Assumes the API serves a purpose not fully aligned with the original collection purpose or declared legal basis.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact subnode depends on the governing obligation involved (purpose limitation, consent, transparency, etc.).

title: Stored profile images may enable linkage across accounts or contexts
description: Persisting uploaded profileImage files in a filesystem-backed image store can create a stable identifier if filenames, paths, hashes, or image contents are reused or accessible across services or tenants. The same image may be linked to the same person across different accounts, sessions, or datasets.
assumptions: The image store or its metadata may be accessible to multiple backend components, admins, logs, backups, or downstream processors; filenames or derived identifiers may be retained.
uncertainty_note: Node id is my best fit for linkability via persistent identifiers in stored content; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree wording may differ.

title: Stored profile images can reveal identity directly
description: A profileImage often contains a face or other directly identifying visual traits. Storing it in backend/uploads/images makes the data store a repository of directly identifying personal data, enabling identification of the user if accessed by unauthorized parties or used outside the original purpose.
assumptions: Uploaded images may contain the user's face or other unique attributes; unauthorized internal or external access is possible.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identification from stored content; exact subtree label may vary.

title: Profile images may disclose sensitive personal information
description: Images can contain special-category or otherwise sensitive information, such as health indicators, religious symbols, location clues, family members, or biometric facial data. Storage in the filesystem increases the risk of disclosure if access controls, segregation, or retention are inadequate.
assumptions: Users may upload arbitrary photos, not only sanitized avatars; the filesystem may be backed up, replicated, or exposed through misconfiguration.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node; precise LINDDUN Pro node may differ depending on whether biometric/special-category data is modeled explicitly.

title: Insufficient proof of image upload consent or action
description: If /api/auth stores a profileImage without robust audit records tied to the user action, the system may be unable to prove whether the user uploaded, replaced, or approved the stored image. This creates repudiation risk for the upload event and associated privacy choices.
assumptions: Audit logging, timestamps, user identifiers, and integrity protection for upload events may be incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit repudiation node for user action logging; exact node numbering may differ.

title: Users may be unaware that profile images are stored in backend filesystem storage
description: The flow stores uploaded profileImage data into backend/uploads/images, but users may not understand where it is stored, how long it is retained, who can access it, or whether it is reused for moderation, analytics, backups, or account recovery. This undermines transparency and informed expectations.
assumptions: Privacy notices or UI disclosures may not clearly explain storage location, retention, backup handling, and secondary uses.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness/transparency node; exact LINDDUN Pro numbering may vary.

title: Storing uploaded profile images may exceed consented or expected purpose
description: A user may provide a profileImage expecting only account display functionality, while the backend stores it in a general filesystem location that could support additional uses such as backups, admin review, content moderation, model training, or cross-service reuse. If those uses are not covered by consent or another valid legal basis, the storage operation may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Purpose limitation, retention limits, and legal basis for all downstream uses are not fully enforced or documented.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node related to consent, purpose limitation, and retention; exact node id may differ.

title: Stored ID images expose highly sensitive attributes
description: The file system stores uploaded identity document images, which may contain full name, photo, date of birth, document number, nationality, address, and other sensitive personal data. If the storage location is accessible beyond a strict need-to-know basis, the persisted files disclose more personal information than necessary to parties who can access the store.
assumptions: Uploaded idImage files are retained on disk in backend/uploads/images and may be accessible to administrators, backup operators, or compromised components.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure from data at rest; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary.

title: Consistent file storage may enable linkability across submissions
description: If uploaded ID images are stored with stable filenames, predictable paths, or metadata that reference the same account, an attacker or internal party with access to the file system could correlate multiple uploads to the same individual or link the image to other records.
assumptions: File names, directory structure, timestamps, or metadata may embed user identifiers or otherwise remain stable across events.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for linkability via stored identifiers/metadata.

title: Stored ID images can directly identify the data subject
description: An identity document image usually directly reveals the data subject through portrait, name, document number, and other unique attributes. Anyone obtaining access to backend/uploads/images may be able to identify the person without needing additional data.
assumptions: The uploaded image is a real identity document or similar image containing direct identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from directly identifying content in stored files.

title: Unclear retention of ID images may prevent deletion
description: If idImage files are written to the file system without a defined lifecycle, users may be unable to have the images deleted when no longer necessary, or copies may persist in caches, backups, or orphaned directories. This undermines the ability to exercise deletion-related rights.
assumptions: The implementation may not automatically purge files, remove backup copies, or track all stored instances.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for deletion difficulties due to unmanaged persistent storage.

title: Storing full ID images on the file system may exceed purpose limitation or data minimization
description: Persisting complete identity-document images in a backend uploads directory may process more personal data than is necessary for the intended subprofile function, especially if only selected attributes or a transient verification result are needed. This creates risk of non-compliance with minimization, storage limitation, and purpose-limitation obligations.
assumptions: The business purpose may be satisfiable with fewer attributes, redaction, extraction, or shorter retention than full-image storage.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance related to excessive collection/retention; exact subtree may differ.

title: Insufficient evidence of upload and storage actions may enable repudiation
description: If the API process stores the uploaded idImage without reliable audit records, the user or operator may later dispute whether a specific image was uploaded, replaced, or deleted. Missing provenance for storage events weakens accountability for this privacy-sensitive processing.
assumptions: The process may lack tamper-resistant logs capturing who uploaded which file, when, and under what consent or policy basis.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for repudiation/accountability around storage events.

title: Stored uploaded videos may reveal sensitive personal information
description: Uploaded video files stored in backend/uploads can contain directly identifying or highly sensitive content such as faces, voices, location cues, documents, biometric traits, or information about bystanders. If the storage is accessed by unauthorized parties or reused beyond the user's expectations, the stored content can disclose personal information.
assumptions: The application permits user-uploaded videos that may contain personal data and stores them persistently on the server file system.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id chosen from common LINDDUN Pro disclosure threats; exact subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Persistent video storage enables linkability across uploads or users
description: If uploaded videos are stored with stable filenames, directory structures, metadata, uploader identifiers, or reusable references, records in backend/uploads may be linkable across sessions, uploads, or accounts. This can allow observers or insiders to correlate multiple videos to the same individual or household.
assumptions: Stored files or associated storage metadata preserve stable identifiers or attributes over time.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers in stored data.

title: Stored videos may allow identification of uploader or recorded individuals
description: Even if the system does not explicitly label a video with a person’s name, the content and metadata of stored videos can allow identification of the uploader or other people appearing in the footage through visible faces, voices, surroundings, timestamps, or embedded metadata.
assumptions: Videos may contain recognizable persons or metadata retained during upload and storage.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/identifiability node id; exact numbering may differ between LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Video retention in backend/uploads may exceed user consent or stated purpose
description: The flow stores uploaded videos in backend/uploads, potentially for longer than necessary or for purposes broader than users expect. If retention, reuse, moderation, analytics, or sharing are not aligned with consent and notice, storage may violate user privacy expectations and regulatory requirements.
assumptions: Retention limits, purpose limitation, or explicit consent controls may be absent or insufficiently enforced for stored uploads.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node id based on storage/retention and purpose-limitation concerns; exact subtree may vary.

title: Lack of reliable upload logging could prevent accountability for stored videos
description: If /api/videos stores files in backend/uploads without trustworthy audit records of who uploaded what and when, users or operators may later be unable to prove or dispute actions related to a stored video. This undermines accountability and may complicate privacy incident response or data subject requests.
assumptions: The upload process may not create tamper-resistant logs tied to the stored file.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation applicability depends on whether accountability/audit requirements are in scope for this flow; node id is best-effort.

title: Users may be unaware that uploaded videos are stored on server file system
description: People uploading videos may not understand that their files are persisted in backend/uploads, possibly with metadata intact, backups, and retention beyond immediate processing. This lack of transparency can prevent informed privacy decisions about what content they submit.
assumptions: The system's UI or privacy notice may not clearly disclose server-side storage, retention, or subsequent handling of uploaded videos.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness node id; exact numbering may vary with the threat-tree edition.

title: Broad file-system access could make uploaded videos available to unauthorized parties
description: If backend/uploads is not adequately isolated, protected, or access-controlled, uploaded videos may become accessible to administrators, other services, backup operators, or attackers beyond what is necessary. This amounts to unauthorized dissemination or exposure of private video content.
assumptions: Stored files may be reachable through shared infrastructure, weak permissions, or misconfigured serving paths.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure/dissemination node id for unauthorized access to stored data; exact numbering may differ by catalog.
